 Truecaller AB (TRUBF) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Return to Constant-Currency Growth ...
 GuruFocus News Tue, November 3, 2026 at 3:03 PM CST 8 min read TRUE-B.ST -15.16% 
 TRUBF 0.00% 
 This article first appeared on GuruFocus . 
 Net Sales: Decreased 1% YoY in SEK; grew 3% YoY in constant currency; up 18% QoQ. 
 EBITDA: Decreased 9% YoY in SEK (5% in constant currency), excluding SEK18 million non-recurring TextPlus advisory costs; margin of 32%. 
 Gross Profit: Down 7% YoY in SEK; up 17% QoQ. 
 Gross Margin: 72%, pressured by higher own ads infrastructure costs and temporary verification price hikes. 
 Ad Revenue: Down 12% YoY (15% in SEK); strong sequential growth of 23% QoQ. 
 Premium Subscription Revenue: Grew 32% YoY; subscribers up ~23% YoY to 4.06 million; conversion rate up ~16% YoY. 
 Truecaller for Business Net Sales: Grew 6% YoY in SEK, 14% in constant currency; ARR up 3% in SEK (8% in constant currency). 
 Business Messaging: Delivered 18% more messages than same period last year. 
 Recurring Revenue: Grew 26% YoY in constant currency. 
 Operating Cash Flow: SEK157 million, excluding paid income tax and working capital changes, vs SEK177 million a year ago. 
 Cash Position: SEK1.3 billion in cash and short-term investments; SEK450 million net of SEK850 million term loan. 
 Working Capital: Change of SEK33 million year-to-date; accounts receivable trend stable. 
 Tax Rate: Group tax rate of 37%, elevated by non-deductible TextPlus advisory costs. 
 Tax Provision: SEK92 million provision for potential Indian transfer pricing exposure (gross claims ~SEK900 million; net exposure ~SEK550 million worst case). 
 TextPlus Contribution: ~SEK3 million in net sales since September 10 closing. 
 Average MAU: 476 million, up 8% YoY; 5 million net adds in the quarter, 35 million YoY. 
 Average DAU: 411 million, up 8% YoY; DAU-to-MAU ratio of 86%.

 Positive Points 
 Truecaller AB ( TRUBF ) returned to year-on-year growth in constant currency, with net sales up 3% and all three revenue streams growing sequentially. 
 Premium subscriptions continued strong momentum, with revenues up 32% year-on-year and subscriber base growing 23% to 4.06 million. 
 Advertising revenue showed significant sequential recovery, growing 23% quarter-over-quarter, and the new auction-based bidding model is scaling. 
 Truecaller for Business returned to growth, with recurring revenues up 26% year-on-year in constant currency and business messaging volumes up 18%. 
 The TextPlus acquisition and eSIM expansion open new growth avenues, including ownership of phone numbers and entry into the US market. 
 Story Continues Negative Points 
 User growth slowed to 5 million net adds in Q3, the slowest in recent quarters, due to a global decline in smartphone shipments. 
 Net sales decreased 1% year-on-year in SEK terms, and EBITDA fell 9% year-on-year, impacted by currency headwinds and non-recurring costs. 
 Advertising revenues declined 12% year-on-year, though the decline was less severe than in previous quarters. 
 Truecaller AB ( TRUBF ) faces a potential tax claim of approximately SEK900 million from Indian authorities, with a provision of SEK92 million and a possible net exposure of SEK550 million. 
 The company expects continued deceleration in user growth in the near term, as smartphone shipments are projected to remain weak. 
 Q & A Highlights 
 Q : Why did Truecaller book a SEK92 million tax provision if management still believes the company has done nothing wrong on transfer pricing? A : CFO Odd Bolin said accounting regulations require the company to quantify potential risk even while it defends its position. He noted the Indian authorities have made a claim, Truecaller has strong counter-arguments, and the company will keep fighting for zero, but it cannot assume the Swedish authorities will bring the exposure to zero. The SEK92 million is described as a prudent provision covering all years under audit, not a recurring quarterly item, against a gross claim expected to reach roughly SEK900 million and a possible net exposure of about SEK550 million after Swedish tax refunds. 
 Q : What is the status and expected timeline of the Indian transfer pricing dispute, and how will the bank guarantee affect the balance sheet? A : CFO Odd Bolin said Truecaller has received the first formal transfer pricing order and expects an assessment order soon, which would likely require a bank guarantee of about SEK270 million, eventually rising to roughly SEK900 million. The guarantee must stay in place until the matter is settled, most likely through the bilateral process with Swedish tax authorities, which is expected to conclude no earlier than late 2027 or during 2028. He stressed the company has SEK1.3 billion in cash and short-term investments, or SEK450 million net of its SEK850 million term loan, so it can handle the guarantee without disrupting the business. 
 Q : Why did user growth slow to 5 million net adds in Q3, and will this affect financial performance? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala attributed the slowdown primarily to a dramatic drop in global smartphone shipments, estimated more than 20% lower in Q3 versus 2025 as rising memory chip prices made devices more expensive. Preloads of Truecaller also trended lower because OEMs shipped fewer devices, not because budgets were cut. The impact is concentrated in established, well-penetrated markets where growth depends on first-time smartphone buyers, while regions with lower penetration and better ARPU are growing healthily. He warned the deceleration will likely continue in the near term, with Q4 typically the strongest device-selling period, but said it does not affect the financial trajectory. 
 Q : How is the advertising business performing, and what progress has been made on the ad stack transformation? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala said ads revenue grew 23% sequentially, though it was still down 12% year on year in constant currency, a much slower decline than prior quarters. The company is serving fewer impressions at higher quality across both programmatic and direct sales. The entire user base has moved to the new architecture, and the new auction-based bidding model has scaled to about 10% of users, with further rollout expected in Q4. He said September marked year-on-year growth in ads, and the company is now positioned as a publisher of choice for brands seeking scale, quality and brand safety. 
 Q : What drove the strong premium subscription growth, and which markets are outperforming? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala said premium revenue grew 32% year on year, subscribers rose about 23% to 4.06 million, and conversion rates improved about 16% year on year, with better conversion on both Android and iOS versus the prior quarter. He cited Colombia, where revenue doubled year on year and rose 25% quarter on quarter; South Africa, up 60% year on year and 13% sequentially; Malaysia, up 50% year on year and more than 10% sequentially; Nigeria, which more than doubled; and Mexico, up 70% year on year. He called geographic diversification a cornerstone of future strategy. 
 Q : How is Truecaller for Business performing, and what is the outlook for business messaging? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala said Truecaller for Business net sales grew 6% year on year in SEK and 14% in constant currency, with strong sequential growth. Verified business ARR rose 3% in SEK and 8% in constant currency with churn unchanged, while business messaging volumes grew 18% year on year as both the returning long-standing exclusive partner and new partners scaled up. CFO Odd Bolin added that recurring revenues are back on track, growing 26% year on year in constant currency, and that TextPlus and eSIM are now included in recurring revenues and expected to contribute more over time. 
 Q : What is the strategic rationale for the TextPlus acquisition, and what has it contributed so far? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala said TextPlus, a second phone number service for calls and texting in the US on iOS and Android, aligns with three focus areas: recurring revenue, since 80% of its revenue comes from premium subscriptions that were already growing; geographic diversification into valuable markets; and product expansion made possible by owning the phone number itself, similar to a telco. He said this creates a large potential footprint and a differentiated global offering. CFO Odd Bolin noted TextPlus contributed about SEK3 million to net sales since closing on September 10, and the deal carried SEK18 million in non-recurring advisory costs. 
 Q : What caused the year-on-year decline in net sales and EBITDA, and how did margins hold up? A : CFO Odd Bolin said net sales fell 1% in SEK but grew 3% in constant currency, while EBITDA excluding non-recurring items fell 9% in SEK and 5% in constant currency, with a 32% margin in both. The decline in ads was more than offset by growth in premium and Truecaller for Business, but a strong Swedish krona versus the dollar and rupee continued to weigh on results. He noted quarter-over-quarter net sales improved 18% and gross profit rose 17%, with the 72% gross margin reflecting higher costs for the company's own ad servers and some temporary verification price hikes. 
 Q : Will the mandatory full-scale CNAP rollout across Indian operators from November 1 have a material impact on premium or business revenue in Q4? A : CEO Rishit Jhunjhunwala said CNAP has been rolled out substantially since Q4 of last year, and the November 1 date was mandated for full-scale rollout. Since then, the company has not seen CNAP change its business and does not expect a material impact from the full rollout.
